module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil
public import FormalConjectures.Wikipedia.Hadamard

/-!
# The circulant Hadamard conjecture

A circulant matrix is generated by cyclically shifting one row. The circulant Hadamard conjecture,
also attributed to Ryser, says that no circulant Hadamard matrix has order greater than $4$.

*Reference:*
* S. Steinerberger,
  [A note on approximate Hadamard matrices](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.13202)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace CirculantHadamard

/-- A generator for a circulant Hadamard matrix of order four. -/
def orderFourGenerator : Fin 4 → ℝ :=
  ![1, 1, 1, -1]

/-- The order-four generator gives a circulant Hadamard matrix. -/
@[category test, AMS 15]
theorem orderFourGenerator_isHadamard :
    Hadamard.IsHadamard' (Matrix.circulant orderFourGenerator) := by
  constructor
  · intro i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      norm_num [Matrix.circulant, orderFourGenerator, Fin.sub_def, Fin.neg_def]
  · ext i j
    fin_cases i <;> fin_cases j <;>
      norm_num [Matrix.mul_apply, Matrix.circulant, orderFourGenerator, Fin.sum_univ_succ,
        Fin.sub_def, Fin.neg_def, Matrix.ofNat_apply]

/-- Every circulant Hadamard matrix has order at most four. -/
@[category research open, AMS 15]
theorem circulant_hadamard_conjecture {n : ℕ} (v : Fin n → ℝ)
    (hv : Hadamard.IsHadamard' (Matrix.circulant v)) : n ≤ 4 := by
  sorry

end CirculantHadamard

reformulations.difference: The paper defines Hadamard matrices using ±1 entries and pairwise-orthogonal rows. Lean uses the column-Gram condition M.transpose * M = ↑n and states the conjecture as an upper bound on the order.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The matrix cast ↑n is n times the identity. A circulant's transpose is circulant, and circulants commute, so MᵀM = MMᵀ. With ±1 entries, every row has squared length n; thus MMᵀ = nI is equivalent to pairwise orthogonality of distinct rows. Finally, every such matrix having n ≤ 4 is equivalent to nonexistence for n > 4. Both the Hadamard-predicate equivalence and the full conjecture equivalence were proved without sorry in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

sources_consulted: S. Steinerberger, A Note on Approximate Hadamard Matrices, arXiv:2402.13202v1, full LaTeX source (especially abstract and §§1.1, 1.3, 3.3): https://arxiv.org/e-print/2402.13202

Local definitions: FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/Hadamard.lean; Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Matrix/Circulant.lean; Mathlib/Data/Matrix/Diagonal.lean; Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Fin/Basic.lean; Lean Init/Data/Fin/Basic.lean.
review.notes: All three declarations were checked. Matrix.circulant uses modular subtraction and exactly matches the paper's displayed circulant convention. The order-four generator is valid, and its theorem has no sorry dependency. Lean checks confirmed the n=0 and n=1 cases; allowing n=0 is harmless since 0 ≤ 4. Exhaustive integer sign-vector tests for orders 0–8 found circulant Hadamard matrices only at orders 0, 1, and 4. The cited paper and consulted Wikipedia section continue to describe the main claim as a conjecture. The reviewed file was not modified.
